title: HTTP Fundamentals and Standard-Library API Requests

understand.concept: An HTTP API lets a client exchange requests and responses with a server. Python's urllib.request can issue HTTP requests using the standard library. A client should set an appropriate method and headers, handle status and transport errors, decode response bytes using the declared encoding and parse structured payloads. Network examples are environment-dependent and should not be assumed to work in an offline browser playground.
understand.whyItMatters: API integration allows Python applications to use external services while keeping request handling explicit and testable.
understand.analogy: An API request is a structured order sent to a service desk; the response reports what the service could do.
understand.analogyLimit: The service may be unavailable, slow, rate-limited or return unexpected data, and a successful HTTP response can still contain invalid application data.
understand.summary: HTTP Fundamentals and Standard-Library API Requests develops practical application engineering skills for Python projects.

explain.narrative:
## Build an explicit HTTP client
Use `urllib.request.Request` to describe a request and `urlopen` with a timeout to send it. Handle `HTTPError` for HTTP error responses and `URLError` for transport failures. Read and decode response bytes, then parse JSON only after checking the response. Never put API secrets in source code or log authorization headers. The examples construct and inspect request objects locally; they do not depend on a live external service.

examples.title: Construct a GET request
examples.code:
from urllib.request import Request
request = Request('https://api.example.test/items', method='GET')
print(request.get_method())
examples.explanation: Request objects can be prepared and inspected without making a network call.

examples.title: Set an Accept header
examples.code:
from urllib.request import Request
request = Request('https://api.example.test/items', headers={'Accept': 'application/json'})
print(request.get_header('Accept'))
examples.explanation: The Accept header communicates the preferred response format.

examples.title: Build a POST request body
examples.code:
from urllib.request import Request
body = b'{"name":"Asha"}'
request = Request('https://api.example.test/users', data=body, headers={'Content-Type': 'application/json'})
print(request.get_method(), len(body))
examples.explanation: Providing data makes the default request method POST; the body is bytes.

examples.title: Encode query parameters
examples.code:
from urllib.parse import urlencode
query = urlencode({'page': 2, 'search': 'blue pen'})
print(query)
examples.explanation: urlencode safely encodes query parameter values.

examples.title: Classify common network exceptions
examples.code:
from urllib.error import HTTPError, URLError
print(issubclass(HTTPError, URLError))
examples.explanation: HTTPError is a specialized URLError and can be handled before its parent.

practise.guidedTask: Construct a GET request with an Accept header and encoded query parameters. Add a timeout and describe HTTPError and URLError handling.
practise.independentTask: Design an API client interface that separates request construction, transport, response decoding and payload validation.
